text:
maya: Heads-up: sales flagged 3 renewals that hinge on routing guarantees + residency. We need a concise product roadmap and launch criteria to share.

tom: Can we frame it as three deliverables: primitives, operational guarantees, and premium isolation?

sana: I like that. Primitives = policy knobs (latency, geo, cost), tenant hints, sticky affinity. Ops guarantees = runbooks, canary plan, SLIs. Premium = reserved lanes + data residency + pricing uplift.

jules: For timelines: primitives in 60d, ops guarantees + canary in 120d, premium lanes 6-9 months. Need to be explicit about gating conditions.

keiko: Gating from Ops: capacity approval, telemetry hooks emitted, rollback automation present, and a chaos-tested canary for 7 days.

maya: Sales asks: 1) per-region data residency, 2) p99 tail latency target, 3) ability to opt into dedicated capacity.

tom: Proposed canary spec: 7d, 5% traffic, two region pairs, metric pass: p95/p99 within 10% of baseline, error-rate delta <0.5%.

sana: Launch criteria draft bullet list:
- Canary completed and passed
- Compatibility matrix for top 5 model families published
- Runbook & rollback steps validated in a drill
- Pricing uplift agreed with finance for premium lanes

jules: Compatibility matrix note: include quantization formats and kernel availability. This will determine which tenants can be offered reserved lanes.

keiko: Ops telemetry list: policy_decision, route_selected, route_fallback, kv_sync_status. Each event must carry tenant_id and policy_id.

sales-bot: Deal impact: these features could convert 2 enterprise prospects this quarter if timelines are met.

maya: Action items: Sana owns the one-pager with phases + gating criteria (due in 5 business days). Jules to scope the compatibility spike (10 days). Keiko to draft telemetry contract. Tom will coordinate SLAs with finance.

sana: Will do. Ill include example policy payload and a stubbed acceptance test matrix.

keiko: One more: include evacuation window and soft-eviction rules (e.g., degrade to smaller model family, or spill to global pool) in the runbook.

jules: Noted. Also recommend a short customer-facing FAQ covering "what happens during overflow" and "how pricing changes."

maya: Great. I'll schedule a 30m review next Tue to sign off on the one-pager before it goes to sales. Thanks all.
